relevance_note: Table 1 is a catalogue of ITGB2 mutations in LAD-I patients, each tied to patients identified by database accession number ("an LAD-I, LAD-II and LAD-III database that lists these patients by accession number"), so each accession number is an identifiable person with an individual-level fact (their variant).
method_note: Mutation-catalogue update (LAD-I/II/III). Only Table 1 (ITGB2) is in scope; Tables 3-4 (SLC35C1, FERMT3; LAD-II/III) and Table 2 (ITGB2 polymorphisms, not tied to persons) give no rows. Each patient accession number in Table 1's 'Accession Number' column (the text says the database 'lists these patients by accession number') is one individual, labelled by that number (rule 1); a person listed in two Table 1 rows gets both variants. A Python script transcribed Table 1 (87 rows, 127 accession numbers, 161 person-variant rows); I checked its output against the table. Spans for each person/variant are the Table 1 row segment from the nucleotide cell through the accession cell. The row 'Not identified | Splice site | Deletion exon 13 p.Gly553AlafsX6' has no accession number, so no person was created for it, nor for families in the 'Families (alleles)' counts that have no accession number. Not recorded: zygosity (the 'Families (alleles)' counts and footnote b 'One or more patients presumed to be homozygous' are row-level and hedged, so not attributed to a person); inheritance and parental testing (not stated); transcript (the paper gives cDNA numbering with +1 at the ATG and mentions GenBank M15395 with a 72-nt offset, but does not give an NM_ transcript, so 'not reported'); footnote c 'reverse mutations in a small subset of lymphocytes [32]' (row-level somatic reversion, not attributed to a person). variant_type: Missense/Nonsense/Splice site map directly; 'Deletion | Entire gene' maps to large deletion/CNV; other 'Deletion', 'Insertion' and 'Deletion/insertion' map to 'other' (frameshift not derived from the p. string); hedged classes ('Splice site?', 'Deletion? Splice site?', 'Deletion or splice site') are 'not reported'. functional_evidence_statement comes from the 'LAD-I type' cell plus the legend defining ^o/^-/^+ (CD18 expression on patients' leukocytes by flow cytometry, sometimes on transfected COS cells); LAD-I^? ('not known') is 'not reported'. disease_label_as_stated is that LAD-I type cell. source_reference_in_review copies the row's Reference cell; in rows listing several accession numbers that cell covers all of them, and they were not split by position. No phenotypic features are given per person, so phenotypic_features is empty and every checklist item is 'not reported'. Contradiction: c.2147G>C (p.Gly716Ala, A0054) is listed as a missense mutation in Table 1 (footnote f: 'Not certain of clinical significance') and also as a polymorphism in Table 2. c.1756C>T (p.Arg586Trp), found in two unnamed patients on the same allele as c.742-14C>A, is treated by the authors as a polymorphism and is not attributed to an accession number, so no row. Accession numbers A0001-A0009 also appear in Table 3 (SLC35C1, LAD-II) for different patients; only the Table 1 (ITGB2) numbers are used here.

study_type.span: In the present publication, 53 newly identified mutations have been added to Table 1 (marked with * in the last column).
